Know

What is Learning Journeys?

Understand the PMM role in building and sustaining a learning culture across the function.

Overview

What this area is

Learning Journeys is the practice of designing and delivering the curriculum, modules, and development pathways that build PMM capability across the function. PMM supports this area by contributing product and market expertise to curriculum development, identifying skill gaps, and ensuring learning content reflects the real demands of the role — especially as AI reshapes what excellent PMM work looks like.

Responsibilities

What this PMM area is accountable for doing.

  • Design and maintain the PMM learning pathway and curriculum map
  • Develop or commission module content with clear learning objectives
  • Maintain content currency as the market and tools evolve
  • Support certification and skill assessment processes

Needs PMM validation

Key deliverables

The artifacts and outputs PMM is expected to produce.

  • Learning curriculum and pathway map
  • Module content library
  • Certification criteria and assessment framework
  • Skill gap analysis and learning priorities

Needs PMM validation

Collaborators & interlocks

Who you work with and what each interlock requires.

  • L&D → programme design and delivery infrastructure
  • HR → certification recognition and career framework integration
  • Field → skill gap input and learning priority validation
  • Product → content accuracy and technical review

Needs PMM validation

Inputs required

What you need before you can execute this work well.

  • PMM skill gap analysis and field performance data
  • Product and market update requirements
  • Field training needs from manager surveys
  • Learning engagement and completion metrics from prior modules

Needs PMM validation

Playbook
1

Assess skill gaps

Analyse field performance data and survey PMMs to identify the most critical knowledge and capability gaps. Separate what field teams need now from what will matter in 12 months.

2

Design learning pathway

Structure a logical curriculum from foundational to advanced. Align the pathway to the PMM career framework so learners understand where each module fits in their development.

3

Develop module content

Write or commission module content with a clear learning objective and a practice exercise for each module. Prioritise relevance over comprehensiveness.

4

Launch and measure

Publish modules and track completion rates, drop-off points, and qualitative feedback. Identify the modules that learners complete vs. the ones they abandon.

5

Iterate based on performance data

Use completion rates, knowledge retention scores, and field performance correlation to decide which modules to update, expand, or retire.

KPIs
Completion
Module completion rate
% of enrolled PMMs completing each module within the target timeframe after enrolment.
Retention
Knowledge retention score
Average score on post-module assessments taken 30 days after completion.
Impact
Training impact on field performance
Correlation between module completion and measurable field performance outcomes (deal quality, message accuracy, etc.).
Achievement
Certification rate
% of PMMs achieving certification in the modules where a certification pathway is available.
